dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: A predicate asserting that for every real threshold t, the probabilities assigned by the laws of X i to (-∞, t] tend along l to the corresponding probability for Z.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the left-hand proposition of the equivalence and its displayed definition is exactly the right-hand convergence condition.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002

binders: Ω is an arbitrary type equipped with a measurable space.
ι is an arbitrary index type.
μ is a probability measure on Ω.
X is an ι-indexed family of real-valued functions on Ω.
l is a filter on ι.
Z is a real-valued function on Ω.
hX supplies, for every i : ι, almost-everywhere measurability of X i with respect to μ.
hZ supplies almost-everywhere measurability of Z with respect to μ.
hypotheses: The measure μ has total mass one.
Every function X i is almost-everywhere measurable with respect to μ.
The function Z is almost-everywhere measurable with respect to μ.
conclusions: LocalDef001 μ X l Z hX hZ is logically equivalent to the assertion that, for every real t, the probability that X i lies in (-∞, t] tends along l to the probability that Z lies in (-∞, t].
mathematical_definitions: For an almost-everywhere measurable real-valued function Y, LocalDef002 Y is its distribution: the pushforward probability measure Measure.map Y μ.
For t ∈ ℝ, Set.Iic t is the event {x ∈ ℝ | x ≤ t}.
The value LocalDef002 Y (Set.Iic t) is the nonnegative-real probability μ({ω | Y(ω) ≤ t}), understood through the pushforward law.
Convergence is filter convergence in NNReal to the neighborhood filter of the limiting probability.
LocalDef001 is defined by the same universal pointwise convergence condition displayed on the right-hand side of the equivalence.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For a family of almost-everywhere measurable real-valued random variables X i and an almost-everywhere measurable real-valued random variable Z on a probability space, the predicate LocalDef001 holds if and only if, at every real threshold t, the probabilities P(X i ≤ t) converge along the filter l to P(Z ≤ t).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The equivalence is an unfolding of LocalDef001, so it does not independently prove a substantive convergence theorem.
The condition is imposed at every real threshold t; no restriction to continuity points of the limiting lower-tail function appears.

The index filter l is completely arbitrary. Degenerate filters can make the convergence condition unusually weak or vacuous, while other filters encode sequences, nets, or different modes of approach.
Only almost-everywhere measurability is required; the construction uses pushforward measures defined from such functions.
The statement concerns only probabilities of lower closed intervals and does not itself assert convergence of expectations, moments, densities, samples, or almost-sure values.
Because random variables differing only on a μ-null set induce the same mapped measure, the condition is insensitive to such modifications.
ambiguities: The packet gives no additional intended interpretation of the arbitrary filter l beyond its formal role in Filter.Tendsto.
The conventional name of the convergence notion represented by LocalDef001 is intentionally unavailable; the translation therefore describes only its explicit mathematical content.

The precise implementation behavior of Measure.map on nonmeasurable representatives is not expanded here, although the supplied almost-everywhere measurability assumptions are exactly those required by LocalDef002.
